description: The chart is a horizontal stacked bar chart illustrating the average percentage of attention allocated to three input segments during generation (Context, Generated Response, and Other) for two model conditions. The vertical axis contains the category labels “Ours” (top) and “Standard” (bottom), and the horizontal axis represents percentage composition on a linear scale (0–100%), with each bar spanning the full 100% width. Each bar is divided into three color-coded segments as indicated by the legend: blue for “Context,” orange for “Generated Response,” and green for “Other.” For “Ours,” the stacked segments are labeled 60.6% (blue Context), 31.7% (orange Generated Response), and 7.7% (green Other). For “Standard,” the segments are labeled 23.6% (blue Context), 51.1% (orange Generated Response), and 25.3% (green Other). The bars are not shown as sorted by magnitude beyond the displayed top-to-bottom order, and there are no additional visual emphases such as outlines or annotations beyond the percentage labels within each segment.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average rate at which the model attends most to each input segment: context, generated response, or other (e.g., system prompts) during generation. The vertical axis contains the categories labeled 'Ours' and 'Standard,' while the horizontal axis represents the percentage composition. Each bar is divided into three segments, with colors representing different categories: blue for 'Context,' orange for 'Generated Response,' and green for 'Other.' The 'Ours' bar is composed of approximately 60.6% Context (blue), 31.7% Generated Response (orange), and 7.7% Other (green). The 'Standard' bar consists of approximately 23.6% Context (blue), 41.1% Generated Response (orange), and 35.3% Other (green). Notably, the 'Standard' model demonstrates a significant decline in attention to Context compared to the 'Ours' model, while the attention to Other increases substantially. This suggests that the 'Standard' model prioritizes system prompts over contextual information during generation.
